chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who has an ulcer or a wound and is unable to bandage it or wash away its blood. He said: “He prays and does not wash his garment every day except once, for he is not able to wash his garment every hour.”

key_terms.الْقَرْحُ: an ulcer or sore causing ongoing discharge
key_terms.دَمَهُ: his blood from the wound or sore
key_terms.لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ: he is unable; indicating hardship and incapacity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with blood on one’s clothes from a continuous wound?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one afflicted with a persistent wound or ulcer whose blood soils his clothing and cannot be continuously managed. He is permitted to perform salat (prayer) in that state, and he is only required to wash his garment once each day due to hardship and inability.
